issue.notes:
Test Structure & Config Error Handling Research

## 1. Test File Structure
- 18 test files in flat structure under tests/
- tests/integration/scenarios.rs (49k+ lines) - main integration scenarios
- tests/integration.rs is just a 7-line wrapper importing scenarios.rs
- tests/fixtures/ contains test fixtures (transcript JSONL files)

## 2. How Tests Run Claude-Print
Binary execution pattern:
- workspace_bin() resolves paths relative to test binary location
- claude_print() builds Command pre-wired with mock-claude
- run() executes with timeout (30s for binary_e2e, 5s for config tests)
- Captures stdout/stderr + exit code via std::process::Command

Example pattern: claude_print() with --config arg, run() with timeout, assert exit code 2

## 3. Config Error Handling
Location: src/config.rs

Config structure: Defaults { inherit_hooks, model, max_turns, timeout_secs }
- Model names: must start with claude-, max 100 chars
- max_turns: [1, 1000], timeout_secs: [1, 86400]

Error flow:
1. Config::default_path() resolves XDG config location
2. Config::load_or_default() parses TOML with deny_unknown_fields
3. Defaults::validate() checks bounds and naming rules
4. Config errors → Error::Config(String) → ClaudePrintError::Setup → exit code 2

## 4. Test Helpers
Binary execution: workspace_bin(), claude_print(), run(), parse_json()

Library-level helpers (integration/scenarios.rs):
- CaptureWriter - In-memory output capture
- capture() - Creates buffer + writer pair
- read_json() - Parse captured JSON
- assistant_event(), result_event() - Mock event builders
- write_jsonl() - Fixture generation

Fixture helpers: setup_temp_config(), setup_malformed_config(), tempfile::TempDir

## 5. Error Types & Exit Codes
Internal errors (src/error.rs): Error::Config(String), Io, OpenptyFailed, ForkFailed, etc.

User-facing with exit codes:
- Setup(String) → exit 2 (config, binary not found)
- Timeout → exit 124 (GNU timeout convention)
- Interrupted → exit 130 (128 + SIGINT)
- AssistantError(String) → exit 1 (Claude-side errors)

Config error behavior:
- Exit code: always 2 (Setup error)

issue.description:
src/main.rs:145 uses `io::stdin().read_to_end(&mut buffer)` with no size ceiling, creating a memory exhaustion vulnerability. An attacker can pipe gigabytes to stdin and cause OOM.

WHY THIS IS WRONG:
- Plan.md Security T-2 states: "--input-file is resolved to an absolute path and size-checked before use" to bound memory
- --input-file correctly enforces PROMPT_MAX_BYTES (10MB) via prompt.rs::resolve_input_file
- stdin has NO such limit despite being an equivalent prompt source
- This violates the threat model: a `cat /dev/zero | claude-print` invocation exhausts RAM

CODE PATH:
1. main.rs:145 calls `io::stdin().read_to_end(&mut buffer)` (unbounded read)
2. No PROMPT_MAX_BYTES check (unlike --input-file path which calls prompt::resolve_input_file)
3. No early rejection of oversized stdin before slurping

CONTEXT:
- bf-51qv closed EC-4/T-2 for --input-file and positional prompts
- It did NOT cover stdin (bf-51qv predates prompt.rs module; stdin was never fixed)
- prompt.rs PROMPT_MAX_BYTES constant exists but is only used for --input-file

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- stdin must enforce the same 10MB PROMPT_MAX_BYTES ceiling as --input-file
- Reject stdin >10MB with exit 4 (matching existing unreadable-prompt path) or exit 2 (policy rejection, matching --input-file TooLarge)
- Unit test: stdin with >10MB data is rejected before full allocation
- Unit test: stdin at exactly 10MB boundary is accepted
- Verify with `cargo test` and `cargo clippy` (Definition of Done)
issue.notes: Verification complete: this vulnerability was already fixed by commit 7b838f39 on 2026-08-03 (bead bf-5cso). The prompt::read_stdin_with_limit() function enforces PROMPT_MAX_BYTES (10MB) ceiling using bounded chunked reads. Error handling matches acceptance criteria: TooLarge → exit 2, ReadFailed → exit 4. All 4 stdin unit tests pass, including boundary conditions at exactly 10MB. No additional changes needed.
issue.title: stdin memory exhaustion: read_to_end() has no size limit (T-2 security gap)

Depends on child 2 (socket lifecycle) because teardown removes the socket and destroys workers created upstream. The originally reported defect — SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers not setting the shutdown flag — is believed fixed (serve_signal_handler sets SERVE_SIGNALED in src/pool.rs); verify rather than assume. Acceptance: (1) SIGINT and SIGTERM each set observable shutdown state; (2) accept/poll loops stop promptly after the flag; (3) every pooled child is reaped and its descriptors closed with none left behind; (4) a signal landing inside active teardown stays inert (existing named pin must keep passing); (5) binary-level test drives a real daemon to a clean bounded shutdown on signal; (6) full cargo test suite green.
issue.notes:
Verification-only pass, no repair needed — the teardown surface is correct as committed; all six acceptance criteria hold with evidence.

(1) Signal->flag: serve_signal_handler stores only the SERVE_SIGNALED static (async-safe); accept-loop tick relays it into manager.shutdown(). Unit pin serve_signal_delivery_flips_the_observable_flag (src/pool.rs:1629) drives real raise(SIGINT)/raise(SIGTERM) through the installed handler and fails if the store never lands; e2e serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker and serve_sigint_then_sigterm_stops_cleanly_without_respawn prove each signal's daemon-level effect separately.

(2) Prompt stop: accept loop checks the flag before maintain on every <=250ms poll tick (ACCEPT_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS); the warmup event-loop callback checks it on every wakeup and cancels warming. Whole 4-pin stress rounds finish in ~3.5s against a 15s SHUTDOWN_BOUND.

(3) Reaping + descriptors: shutdown_all drains the whole map (all states); destroy_worker closes the pty master, SIGTERMs the process group, polls WNOHANG through the 2s grace, escalates to group SIGKILL, and every path ends in a waitpid-observed reap (EINTR-retried blocking wait; ECHILD tolerated). Surviving descendants swept by kill_surviving_group. Unit pins destroy_worker_reaps_a_sigterm_compliant_child and destroy_worker_escalates_to_sigkill_and_sweeps_surviving_descendants; e2e /proc snapshots after daemon exit; run_closes_the_listener_when_the_accept_loop_ends pins the listener fd. Audited every raw-fd site in pool.rs: the only ownership transfer is the documented master-fd one, closed by destroy_worker.

(4) Mid-teardown signals inert: handlers stay armed and only re-latch the flag; waitpid retries EINTR. Pin serve_repeated_and_second_signals_during_teardown_do_not_wedge_or_respawn holds signals back until 'cleaning up N workers' proves teardown is mid-flight (MOCK_IGNORE_TERM_HUP forces the 2s grace window) and asserts the daemon was alive at each delivery — no vacuous pass.

(5) Binary-level bounded shutdown: the Daemon harness in tests/serve.rs drives the real compiled binary with mock-claude workers to exit 0 within bound on SIGINT and SIGTERM, socket removed, workers gone from /proc, teardown order pinned (last destroy < socket removal < completion).

(6) Full suite green: 610 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored across 31 test binaries, cargo exit code 0 (verified with pipefail, not a truncated pipeline). The four shutdown-critical e2e pins were stress-run 3 extra iterations — 12/12 green, no flake.

Adversarial review found no defect: no double-destroy (released workers leave the map before destroy; a pending Failed notification is never processed after the flag because maintain is a no-op and shutdown_all drains instead); no fd-reuse exposure during teardown (listener closed before shutdown_all, maintain cannot spawn after the flag, no new accepts); atexit cleanup handler does not conflict with the serve signal handlers.

issue.description:
Umbrella slice 3 of 4 for parent claudepr-982a9e59, after claudepr-c8901b8d confirms error paths. The original defect was a wiring attempt whose signal handlers never set the shutdown flag; the committed handler (src/pool.rs serve_signal_handler, install_serve_signal_handlers) flips a serve-mode shutdown flag that the accept loop relays into manager shutdown within ACCEPT_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS. This child independently confirms that mechanism end to end at the binary level and repairs any gap in place.

Acceptance:
- SIGINT and SIGTERM each produce a bounded, clean stop: the daemon stops accepting promptly and exits without hanging.
- A signal followed by a second signal, or repeated signals landing inside active teardown, neither wedge the daemon nor trigger worker respawn.
- The ordinary session path keeps default signal dispositions (install_serve_signal_handlers is serve-only).
- Named binary-level pins pass: serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker, serve_sigint_then_sigterm_stops_cleanly_without_respawn, serve_repeated_and_second_signals_during_teardown_do_not_wedge_or_respawn (tests/serve.rs).
- Full test suite green in one run; repair any red or missing pin in this child, then close.
issue.notes: Verified end to end at the binary level; no repair needed in the mechanism. (1) All three named pins existed in tests/serve.rs and pass: serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker, serve_sigint_then_sigterm_stops_cleanly_without_respawn, serve_repeated_and_second_signals_during_teardown_do_not_wedge_or_respawn. Mechanism confirmed: serve_signal_handler stores SERVE_SIGNALED (SeqCst), the accept loop relays it into manager.shutdown() on its next poll tick (<=250ms ACCEPT_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS), the listener is dropped before teardown, shutdown_all reaps every worker serially (2s SIGTERM grace then SIGKILL), then the socket is removed and exit 0 — pinned by the teardown-order assertions in the pins. The unit pin serve_signal_delivery_flips_the_observable_flag (src/pool.rs) covers handler->flag delivery itself. (2) The one gap was the serve-only acceptance bullet: no binary-level pin, so installing the serve handler unconditionally in main() would silently swallow Ctrl-C on the ordinary path (nothing outside the accept loop reads SERVE_SIGNALED) undetected. Added plain_session_signals_keep_the_session_contract_not_serve_teardown: an ordinary MOCK_SILENT session is signaled after the --verbose child-forked trace (program-order proof the scoped session handlers are installed) and pins exit 130 within bound, the 'interrupted by signal' stderr line, zero pool-daemon markers, and the mock child reaped from /proc — for SIGINT and SIGTERM both. (3) Full suite green in one run: 612 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored across 30 test binaries; cargo fmt --check and clippy --all-targets clean. Committed tests/serve.rs as d7b38d8 and pushed to origin.
issue.title: Verify SIGINT and SIGTERM set observable shutdown state and stop the accept loop promptly

issue.close_reason: Added comprehensive path validation to cwd_to_slug function. The function now returns Result<String> and validates against: path traversal (., ..), components exceeding 255 characters, null bytes, control characters, empty components, consecutive/trailing slashes, and empty/root paths. Added 18 comprehensive tests covering all edge cases. All 216 tests pass.
issue.description:
src/poller.rs:86-88

WHAT IS WRONG:
The cwd_to_slug function does not validate path components:
```rust
pub fn cwd_to_slug(cwd: &str) -> String {
    cwd.trim_start_matches(/).replace(/, "-")
}
```
No validation for:
- Path traversal attempts (.., .)
- Very long path components (>255 chars, exceeds filesystem limits)
- Null bytes or control characters
- Leading/trailing slashes, multiple slashes

WHY IT IS A REAL DEFECT:
- Path traversal like /home/../etc becomes home-..-etc in slug
- Could create directories outside expected hierarchy
- Very long components create excessively long directory names
- No protection against null bytes or control characters
- Derived transcript paths could be invalid or unsafe

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Add tests for paths with .., ., leading/trailing slashes
2. Test with excessively long components (>255 chars)
3. Verify null bytes and control characters are rejected early
4. Ensure resulting slugs are valid directory names on all filesystems
5. Test that derived paths stay within expected hierarchy
issue.title: Missing path component validation in cwd_to_slug

If equivalent coverage already exists outside the documented set, instead document the pinning test in the probes doc's §Maintenance so the spec names its pin like every other contract.

issue.description:
claude-print silently fails in any working directory that has not already been
trusted. Symptom is a bare:

    {"type":"result","subtype":"internal_error","is_error":true,
     "error_message":"claude exited before Stop hook fired"}

with --verbose showing the session die immediately after dismissal:

    phase transition: waiting -> trust-dismissed
    phase transition: trust-dismissed -> prompt-injected
    prompt injected
    (nothing further — child gone)

Cause: claude 2.1.263 renders the trust dialog with the REFUSING option
selected by default. Screen-scraped from a real TUI under a PTY in an untrusted
dir, the caret sits on the first entry:

    Quick safety check: Is this a project you created or one you trust?
    ❯ No, exit
      Yes, I trust this folder
    Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel

claude-print's dismissal confirms the highlighted entry, so it chooses
"No, exit" and claude terminates before doing any work. The phase machine
reports this as a successful "trust-dismissed" transition, which is why the
failure surfaces later and misleadingly as a Stop-hook error.

Reproduced 2026-09-07, cleanly cwd-dependent and not model- or flag-specific:

    cwd=/home/coding/claude-print    exit=0  -> ADAPTER_OK   (already trusted)
    cwd=/home/coding                 exit=0  -> ADAPTER_OK   (already trusted)
    cwd=/home/coding/claude-governor exit=2  -> claude exited before Stop hook

~/.claude.json confirms the discriminator: claude-governor carries
hasTrustDialogAccepted:false, the two working dirs carry true.

Workaround that fully resolves it: pass --pretrust-cwd (writes
hasTrustDialogAccepted:true before launch). Verified exit 0 with a real turn in
the previously failing dir. But that flag is opt-in and defaults off, so the
default behavior is to fail.

Why this is P0: it breaks claude-print in every fresh workspace, which is
exactly the case for fleet dispatch into a new repo. It is the live blocker for
claude-governor's polish-opus pool, whose queue (~/cgov-polish-queue) does not
exist yet and will be untrusted the moment it is created.

Fix: select the trusting entry explicitly rather than confirming whatever is
highlighted — match on the option text ("Yes, I trust this folder") and move
the caret to it before Enter. Do not rely on ordering or on the default: this
regressed precisely because the default changed. If the trusting option cannot
be positively identified, fail loudly with a distinct error rather than
confirming a default that may be "No, exit".

Verification: a run in a directory whose ~/.claude.json entry is absent or has
hasTrustDialogAccepted:false must complete a real turn and exit 0 WITHOUT
--pretrust-cwd. Add a startup-sequence test covering the caret-on-refuse
layout, alongside the existing trust-dialog phrasing tests in
tests/version_compat.rs.

Binaries: post-fix = release build of committed HEAD 5ff31ea (git-archive export, isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR); pre-fix control = installed ~/.cargo/bin/claude-print 0.2.2 built Sep 7 16:10 (predates fix 06e4d97, Sep 12). Both wrap claude 2.1.270. Same fresh dir /data/build/scratch/cp7c2-untrusted-f7Sf5e (mktemp under ~/scratch), ~/.claude.json entry ABSENT before each run, no --pretrust-cwd anywhere. PRE-FIX: exit=2 {subtype:internal_error, is_error:true, error_message:'claude exited before Stop hook fired'}; phases waiting->trust-dismissed (185ms) -> prompt-injected (1190ms) -> prompt injected, then nothing (child gone); entry stayed ABSENT — exact umbrella signature. POST-FIX: exit=0 {subtype:success, is_error:false, result:'PONG-CP7C2', num_turns:1, session b0a4f023-431d-4194-927c-997bce234306}; phases waiting->trust-dismissed (613ms) -> prompt-injected (2660ms) -> prompt injected -> stop received (27232ms) -> transcript read attempt 3; transcript has real assistant turn claude-sonnet-4-6 'PONG-CP7C2'; ~/.claude.json flipped absent->hasTrustDialogAccepted:true in the same run, proving the dialog was genuinely shown and dismissed via the trusting entry. One earlier post-fix attempt hit exit=124 (stop-hook watchdog, default 120s): trust WAS granted (absent->true, 277 output tokens) but the model stalled (lastAPIDuration 115s vs 26s without retries); rerun with --stop-hook-timeout 300 completed in 27s — startup machinery identical (trust-dismissed 594ms, prompt-injected 1839ms), failure was model latency, not trust dismissal. Restore: test-dir key deleted from ~/.claude.json (83 projects before/after; only residual deltas are claude's own numStartups/tipsHistory counters); test dir, build export, session transcripts and backup all removed. Corroborates independent verification on claudepr-0c1be90a (2026-09-13, binary at then-HEAD bfd91c1).

Define NEEDLE detection, source and destination paths, permissions, overwrite behavior, and the no-NEEDLE case, then add hermetic tests and document the contract.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.notes:
Progress (claude-code-glm-5.3-flash-glm-roam-24):

Contract defined in docs/notes/installer-needle-adapter.md (new):
- Detection: `command -v needle` OR an existing ~/.needle/agents dir.
- Source: claude-print.yaml from the dir containing install.sh (the
  checkout) — NOT a release artifact; never downloaded, no checksums.txt
  entry (the one installed file without checksum verification, because it
  is copied from local checkout state, not fetched).
- Destination: ~/.needle/agents/claude-print.yaml; mkdir -p runs before
  the source check, so the dir is created even when the yaml is absent.
- Permissions: install -m 644 — mode 0644 always (repo copy is 0664;
  drifted destination modes are forced back).
- Overwrite: in place, byte-for-byte, no backup copy (hand edits to the
  installed adapter — e.g. the pool --pool-socket opt-in — revert on the
  next install.sh run; documented).
- No-NEEDLE case: leg skipped in silence, ~/.needle never created.
- Missing source (curl | sh shape): documented Note + skip, install
  succeeds.
- Ordering: leg runs after the artifact legs; any earlier failure places
  no adapter and creates no ~/.needle.

Tests added to tests/install_sh.rs (6 new, 18 total in target, all pass):
needle_on_the_path_installs_the_repo_adapter_template_into_the_agents_dir,
an_existing_agents_dir_alone_triggers_the_adapter_leg,
without_needle_the_agents_dir_is_not_created_and_nothing_needle_related_is_printed,
an_existing_adapter_is_overwritten_in_place_at_0644_with_no_backup_copy,
no_adapter_beside_the_script_skips_the_needle_leg_with_a_note,
a_failed_install_places_no_needle_adapter.

Hermeticity note: the existing runner inherits the host PATH, and this
box HAS needle at ~/.local/bin/needle — so `command -v needle` inside
install.sh flipped per host. New tests pin the child PATH to the stub bin
dir + host tool dirs resolved at test time (NixOS: /run/current-system/
sw/bin, not /usr/bin) and panic if a real needle is reachable, so the
no-NEEDLE cases cannot pass vacuously on a NEEDLE-equipped host.

Docs: README (Install ¶, Upgrades-and-rollback cross-link, NEEDLE
integration §) + cross-link in docs/notes/installer-rollback.md +
CHANGELOG Unreleased/Added entry.

Commit: 14f907c (5 files: tests/install_sh.rs, docs/notes/installer-
needle-adapter.md, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/notes/installer-rollback.md).
AGENTS.md deliberately untouched — a concurrent worker's in-flight edit
(landed separately as 2e8ae05) shares that file.

Full-gate verification (cargo build --all-targets && cargo test in a
clean extraction of HEAD) running; will close after it + push.

issue.description:
Split child of claudepr-982a9e59 (umbrella), after the shutdown flag lands. Audit and repair teardown so a stopped daemon leaves nothing behind.

Scope:
- On shutdown every pooled child is reaped: SIGTERM first, SIGKILL after the grace period, and the parent observes each exit so no zombies remain
- Descriptors (pty masters, listener) are closed
- Cleanup removes only the socket this daemon created — never a foreign or pre-existing socket at the same path
- teardown order is: stop accepting, reap children, then remove the socket

Acceptance:
- After SIGTERM, no descendant processes of the daemon survive and no zombie children remain
- The daemon-created socket path no longer exists after exit
- A pre-existing file at the socket path that this daemon never created is left untouched
issue.notes:
Audit + repair of serve-mode teardown, committed as caf0124 on main (pushed to Forgejo origin).

Audited (all paths route through PoolManager::destroy_worker: release_worker, failed-warmup retire in process_warmup_completions, shutdown_all drain):
- Child reaping: destroy_worker now closes the pty master, SIGTERMs the worker's whole process group (login_tty makes every worker a session/group leader, so killpg reaches descendants a bare kill(pid) strands), polls the direct child with WNOHANG through a 2s DESTROY_GRACE, escalates to group SIGKILL if the exit was not observed, and always ends in a blocking waitpid — EINTR-retried so a second SIGINT/SIGTERM during teardown cannot skip the reap (repair made this attempt). Observing the exit in every branch is what keeps zombies at zero.
- Descendants: survivors of the group SIGTERM are SIGKILLed even when the direct child was already reaped (killpg probe+kill is safe post-reap: a pgid cannot recycle while any member exists); bare-pid fallback deliberately only pre-reap, where the unreaped child pins the pid.
- Descriptors: pty master closed exactly once (raw fd owned solely by PoolWorker); listener dropped inside PoolServer::run before it returns, so a returned daemon refuses connections; warmup self-pipes close via OwnedFd; event loop already returns ChildExited on POLLNVAL, so closing a master under a warming thread cannot tight-loop.
- Socket ownership: (dev,ino) identity captured from the path immediately after bind; cleanup() unlinks only when the occupant is still that socket node — a replacement file (inode recycling hardened by the socket-type check) or a never-bound daemon is left untouched. Teardown order is stop accepting -> reap children -> remove socket, pinned by stderr ordering in the e2e test.

Verification: 24 pool unit tests (incl. real-PTY destroy_worker tests: SIGTERM-compliant reap without burning the grace; SIGTERM-immune escalation at full grace with descendant sweep via /proc group scan), 12 serve e2e tests (workers gone from /proc with zombie detection, socket removed, foreign file untouched mid-run, socket removed when a foreign file preceded startup). Full suite 595 passed / 0 failed; cargo fmt --check and clippy --all-targets clean.

Acceptance: (1) no descendants survive and no zombies remain — covered by killpg group sweep + waitpid-always-reaps teardown, pinned by unit + e2e tests; (2) daemon-created socket gone after exit — pinned; (3) pre-existing/foreign file at the path left untouched — pinned (mid-run replacement e2e, never-bound unit test).

Make SIGINT and SIGTERM set shutdown state and bound the server stop path
Add binary-level tests for serve dispatch, bounded shutdown, and child reaping

detail.reason: closed by NEEDLE: shipped-work gate confirmed the work landed but the agent did not close it

Serve-path pool wiring repaired and compiling: all uncommitted pool/event_loop/lib/Cargo wiring preserved and adapted (commit cdb2759 on main, pushed). Fixed 3 E0606 compile errors in the self-pipe writes via the module's own wake_event_loop helper (also clears its dead-code warning), removed an unused-mut warning, formatted. POLLNVAL now exits the event loop like POLLHUP/POLLERR, pinned by a regression test proven to hang if reverted. Exactly one WarmupNotification per warmup attempt on every path; maintain() no-ops once shutdown is requested. cargo check/clippy/fmt clean for the touched files; 564 tests pass, 0 fail.

Verified complete: serve subcommand dispatch (commit 8454cbc, already on origin/main) satisfies all acceptance criteria — validated pool size (0/>256/non-numeric all exit 2 with actionable stderr), 0600 Unix socket with stale-socket replacement, exactly-N worker population, no fall-through to prompt validation, unbindable socket exits 2 before any spawn, and the default stateless path unchanged (binary_e2e 20/20, cli 25/25, bin 9/9, serve e2e 6/6, pool 11/11, fmt+clippy clean).

Verified fixed-as-committed: the SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown defect named here was repaired by commit 8454cbc (serve dispatch). Handler sets SERVE_SIGNALED; accept loop relays it into PoolManager::shutdown() within the 250ms ACCEPT_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS bound; shutdown_all reaps every worker (SIGTERM->waitpid->SIGKILL), closes PTY fds, cleanup() removes only the bound socket path, exit 0; maintain() guard holds (no respawn after the signal). Evidence: tests/serve.rs 6/6; manual SIGINT+SIGTERM e2e vs mock-claude (settled: exit 0 in 0.21s, all workers reaped, socket-only removal, exactly 2 spawns; mid-warmup: warming workers cancelled and destroyed, no respawn, exit 0). No file changes required — verification-only close.

Serve binary tests now pin the full shutdown contract: SIGINT bounded clean stop with multi-worker /proc reaping check, pre-signal worker-snapshot count, teardown-log assertions ('cleaning up N workers', 'Shutdown complete'), and default non-serve path unchanged (exit 0, text stdout, no daemon markers, no socket). Repaired the prior attempt's non-compiling helper mismatch; guarded Daemon::drop against recycled-pid SIGKILL; removed two needless borrows that would fail clippy -D warnings. All acceptance criteria met; rust-verify gate green on iad-ci (cargo-remote-7tjxp) for pushed commit 55d4b65.

detail.title: Harden serve dispatch, exact pool warmup, and 0600 socket handling
Fix signal-driven shutdown so SIGINT and SIGTERM set observable state promptly
Verify child reaping and daemon-owned socket cleanup on shutdown

detail.reason: Serve dispatch audited end to end: committed wiring from 8454cbc intact and correct on every scope bullet (pool-size validation exit 2, exactly-N warmup, 0600 socket, no prompt-validation fall-through, unchanged default path); repaired the one defect found — request-reader EOF check tested the accumulator instead of each read, so truncated client frames hot-spun their connection threads forever, plus unbounded length-prefix allocation; wire format unchanged. Commit 24b41ff on origin/main; full suite, clippy, and fmt all green.

Shutdown signaling verified and pinned: handler-to-flag transition, bounded accept-loop stop, no respawn after flag, SIGINT-then-SIGTERM teardown inertness, ordinary path at default dispositions. Commit 881f18d pushed.

Teardown audited and repaired in caf0124 (pushed to origin/main): every worker teardown SIGTERMs the process group, observes the exit with waitpid (blocking, EINTR-retried), escalates to group SIGKILL past the 2s grace, and sweeps post-reap group survivors; the listener is closed before teardown; socket removal is (dev,ino)-guarded so only the daemon's own socket is ever unlinked; order is stop-accepting -> reap -> remove. Verified by 24 pool unit tests + 12 serve e2e tests incl. real-PTY SIGKILL escalation with descendant sweep and foreign-file ownership; full suite 595 passed / 0 failed, fmt+clippy clean.

Acceptance surface fully pinned: each parent-bead bullet has at least one regression-catching test across tests/serve.rs, src/main.rs, and src/pool.rs; hermetic; cgroup-limited run green; fmt/clippy clean. Committed as b9e5c32 and pushed to origin.

detail.title: Verify serve dispatch, pool population, and socket setup in the built binary
Verify SIGINT and SIGTERM set observable shutdown state and stop the serve loops promptly
Verify bounded shutdown reaps every child and removes only the daemon-owned socket
Audit the binary-level serve test surface against the parent acceptance criteria

detail.reason: All slice-1 acceptance criteria verified against the built binary; everything already held, so no repairs or commits were needed. Tests: cargo test --test serve 15/15 (pinned by serve_dispatch_enters_the_server_path_and_never_validates_a_prompt, serve_rejects_zero_pool_size, serve_rejects_pool_size_above_max, serve_rejects_non_numeric_pool_size, serve_fails_fast_on_unbindable_socket, serve_fails_fast_on_socket_path_with_missing_parent_directory, serve_warms_exactly_requested_workers_then_shuts_down_cleanly, default_non_serve_invocation_is_unchanged) and cargo test --lib pool 30/30 (bind_socket_creates_owner_only_socket, validate_pool_size units). Observed exit codes on target/debug/claude-print with mock-claude: --pool-size 0 -> 2 (must be at least 1); 257 -> 2 (exceeds maximum of 256); abc -> 2 (clap invalid value); unbindable socket -> 2; missing parent dir -> 2; all with actionable stderr naming the flag/path and remediation, and no socket file created. Live daemon --pool-size 2: socket mode 0600, exactly 2 workers spawned and settled ready, SIGINT -> exit 0, Shutdown complete, socket removed, zero orphans. default_non_serve_invocation_is_unchanged passed; plain prompt path unchanged.

Signal slice verified with one gap repaired in commit 3f74af4 (pushed to origin main). Flag delivery for SIGINT and SIGTERM was already pinned by 881f18d's raise-based unit test (passes); bounded loop-stop was pinned by serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker, serve_sigint_then_sigterm_stops_cleanly_without_respawn, and three SIGTERM-only terminate() contracts (all pass). The uncovered half of the acceptance was a repeated/second signal arriving DURING active teardown — the back-to-back test's second signal races in before the accept loop's next tick, so handler-disarm-during-teardown was invisible to the suite. Repaired with MOCK_IGNORE_TERM_HUP (mock survives group SIGTERM + master-close SIGHUP, forcing destroy_worker's full grace + SIGKILL escalation) plus shutdown_daemon_during_teardown and serve_repeated_and_second_signals_during_teardown_do_not_wedge_or_respawn, which lands a repeated SIGINT and a second SIGTERM inside cleanup and pins exit 0 in SHUTDOWN_BOUND, socket removal, /proc-empty reaping, and no respawn. Mutation-checked: disarming handlers at teardown entry fails the pin with a killed daemon; unmutated the full suite is 609 passed / 0 failed across 30 binaries, fmt and clippy clean.

Verification complete, everything already holds — no repair needed, no file changes. Full evidence recorded in the bead notes: serve e2e suite 16/16 green (incl. serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker, serve_sigint_then_sigterm_stops_cleanly_without_respawn, both foreign-file pins, mid-teardown repeat-signal pin) and pool unit pins 15/15 green (destroy_worker reap + SIGKILL escalation with group sweep, all four cleanup ownership guards) at 3f74af4. All five acceptance criteria are pinned by committed tests; only .beads checkpoint churn remains in the tree, which belongs to the dispatch harness, so no commit is manufactured.

Coverage audit done; every parent bullet maps to a named pinning test; one gap found and filled in this slice (commit 5b94fda). Suite green: 306 lib unit + 13 bin unit + 17 serve tests pass (local cgroup fallback; tree carried pre-existing .beads dirt from other workers).

GAP FILLED: the 0600-socket bullet had no named binary-level pin - its only serve.rs assertion was embedded in serve_warms_exactly_requested_workers_then_shuts_down_cleanly, run under whatever umask the CI runner carries, and the dedicated named pins (bind_socket_creates_owner_only_socket, bind_socket_replaces_stale_socket) live in src/pool.rs unit tests, outside the audited surface. Added serve_socket_is_owner_only_regardless_of_umask: spawns the daemon under a cleared umask 000 and requires mode 0600 exactly, so dropping bind_socket's explicit set_permissions or its narrowed-umask bind window fails loudly (0700/0777) regardless of runner environment. No other gaps: no test extension deferred.

BULLET-TO-TEST MAPPING:
1. Dispatch without prompt validation -> tests/serve.rs serve_dispatch_enters_the_server_path_and_never_validates_a_prompt (binds, runs accept/maintain loop, asserts no no-prompt-provided); unit main.rs serve_subcommand_parses_with_compiled_in_defaults + plain_prompt_invocation_does_not_dispatch_serve + positional_after_serve_is_a_subcommand_parse_error; complement tests/binary_e2e.rs no_prompt_exit4 (default path still exits 4 without a prompt, so the paths cannot have merged); the three pool-size rejections also assert no fall-through.
2. Exact pool population -> serve_warms_exactly_requested_workers_then_shuts_down_cleanly (spawn count == 2, no respawn churn) + serve_default_pool_size_warms_one_worker (compiled-in default 1).
3. 0600 socket permissions -> NEW serve_socket_is_owner_only_regardless_of_umask (umask 000 leg) + embedded assertion in the population test; unit support bind_socket_creates_owner_only_socket / bind_socket_replaces_stale_socket.
4. Exit-2 invalid pool size -> serve_rejects_zero_pool_size / serve_rejects_pool_size_above_max / serve_rejects_non_numeric_pool_size (actionable stderr asserted: flag named, bound stated, no socket created); unit validate_pool_size trio.
5. Exit-2 socket setup -> serve_fails_fast_on_unbindable_socket / serve_fails_fast_on_socket_path_with_missing_parent_directory (exact path named, what-to-check stated, zero spawns); plus serve_rejects_missing_claude_binary_before_binding pinning check-before-bind ordering; unit bind_socket_surfaces_unusable_path_as_error / bind_socket_surfaces_missing_parent_as_error.
6. SIGINT and SIGTERM signal flag delivery -> unit pool.rs serve_signal_delivery_flips_the_observable_flag (real raise -> handler -> flag, both signals, commit 881f18d); binary serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker (SIGINT leg) + serve_sigint_then_sigterm_stops_cleanly_without_respawn (both, second inert) + serve_repeated_and_second_signals_during_teardown_do_not_wedge_or_respawn (signals landing mid-teardown stay inert, commit 3f74af4).
7. Prompt bounded stop -> the bounded-exit assertion in Daemon::shutdown_daemon_inner (daemon must exit within SHUTDOWN_BOUND=15s of the signal vs a 250ms accept poll and 2s per-worker SIGTERM grace), exercised by serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker and every shutdown path in the file.
8. Full child reaping -> serve_sigint_stops_bounded_and_reaps_every_worker (pre-signal /proc snapshot of a 2-worker pool, post-exit sweep: neither alive nor zombie) + the SIGKILL-escalated teardown pinned by serve_repeated_and_second_signals_during_teardown_do_not_wedge_or_respawn; unit destroy_worker_reaps_a_sigterm_compliant_child / destroy_worker_escalates_to_sigkill_and_sweeps_surviving_descendants. The teardown-order sub-claim (reap before socket removal) is pinned by the stderr sequence in the SIGINT test. Close-descriptors has no separate binary pin by design: fds close with process exit (exit 0 asserted everywhere), a leak that kept a child alive is caught by the /proc reaping sweep, and the listener close is pinned at unit level by run_closes_the_listener_when_the_accept_loop_ends.
9. Own-socket-only cleanup -> serve_shutdown_leaves_a_foreign_file_at_the_socket_path_untouched (replacement file survives byte-for-byte) + serve_shutdown_removes_its_socket_even_when_a_foreign_file_preceded_it (restart story); unit cleanup quartet (removes own / leaves replacement / no-bind no-op / already-gone tolerant).
10. Unchanged default non-serve behavior -> tests/serve.rs default_non_serve_invocation_is_unchanged (exit 0, text contract, zero daemon markers, no socket) + unit plain_prompt_invocation_does_not_dispatch_serve + tests/binary_e2e.rs default-path pins (no_prompt_exit4, version_flag_exit0_names_claude_print_and_wrapping, default_mode_omits_setting_sources_in_child_argv, dangerously_skip_permissions_flag pair).

Referenced from umbrella claudepr-982a9e59 notes (revision 14).

detail.reason: Verified: all 4 acceptance criteria already held at 0f0ff4b; no repairs needed, no code changes. Binary-level dispatch test, exact-pool-size population tests, and non-serve-unchanged test all present and green; two of them mutation-verified to be real pins (dispatch disable => dispatch test fails in 0.05s with 'no prompt provided', non-serve test keeps passing). Full suite: 610 passed / 0 failed / 4 deliberate ignores.

Verified every socket-lifecycle acceptance bullet against main; all already implemented and pinned, zero repairs required. (1) 0600: bind_socket narrows umask to 0077 across bind + explicit chmod 0600 (src/pool.rs:936); unit pin bind_socket_creates_owner_only_socket + committed binary pin serve_socket_is_owner_only_regardless_of_umask (spawned under umask 000) pass. (2) Stale socket: bind_socket unlinks the existing path first (pool.rs:939); unit bind_socket_replaces_stale_socket passes and a live probe of the compiled binary rebound over a dead socket node (srw------- after), warmed, served, clean stop; a dangling symlink fails fast exit-2 actionable instead of wedging. (3) Ownership-scoped removal: (dev,ino) captured at bind (socket_identity pool.rs:914), cleanup unlinks only on identity+socket-type match (pool.rs:1335); 4 unit pins (created/replacement/never-bound/already-gone) + binary pins serve_shutdown_leaves_a_foreign_file_at_the_socket_path_untouched and serve_shutdown_removes_its_socket_even_when_a_foreign_file_preceded_it pass. (4) Setup failure exits 2 with 'failed to set up pool socket <path>: ...' stderr naming path and what to check; unit ENOTDIR/ENOENT pins + binary tests for both unbindable shapes pass, both proving no worker spawn precedes the abort. (5) Suite green: 306 lib unit + 13 main-bin unit + all integration targets 0 failed (tests/serve.rs 17/17); clippy --all-targets and cargo fmt --check clean. No file changes, so no commit; residual accepted edge (chmod-after-bind leak self-heals on next start) recorded in bead notes.

Verified: signal-driven bounded shutdown and full child reaping are correct as committed; no repair required. All six acceptance criteria hold: (1) SIGINT and SIGTERM each flip SERVE_SIGNALED through the real installed handler (unit pin at src/pool.rs:1629) and each produce the clean-stop contract e2e; (2) accept loop relays the flag within its 250ms tick before maintain, warmup callback cancels on every wakeup; (3) shutdown_all drains all workers and every destroy_worker path ends in a waitpid-observed reap with group-SIGKILL escalation and descendant sweep — pinned at unit level (both destroy_worker pins) and e2e (/proc empty after exit), listener fd close pinned, raw-fd audit clean; (4) mid-teardown signals provably inert (held-back delivery pin, non-vacuous); (5) binary-level tests drive the real daemon to exit 0 within SHUTDOWN_BOUND on both signals with socket removal and reaping checks; (6) full suite 610 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored across 31 binaries with cargo exit 0, plus 3 extra stress iterations of the four shutdown pins, all green. No file changes, so no commit; findings recorded in bead notes.

All five acceptance criteria verified with evidence; one consolidation repair landed. (1) invalid --pool-size exits 2 with actionable stderr: zero/above-max/non-numeric were already pinned at the binary level; the negative-value shape was the one gap — probed the real binary (--pool-size=-1 -> exit 2 naming flag and value, no socket), then added serve_rejects_negative_pool_size (commit 8f381cb, pushed to origin/main). (2) socket bind failure exits 2 with actionable stderr: both unbindable shapes (parent a file, parent missing) pinned asserting the exact path and the what-to-check guidance, no worker spawn before the abort. (3) four-area matrix (command dispatch, clean bounded shutdown, child reaping, default non-serve behavior) complete, named, and green in one cargo test run: exit 0, 611 passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored across 30 test binaries (18/18 in serve.rs). (4) no surviving gap — the single gap found was filled this pass and recorded on parent claudepr-982a9e59, whose notes now carry the child-4 update. (5) default stateless invocation confirmed unchanged (default_non_serve_invocation_is_unchanged + the no-dispatch parse pin). cargo fmt --check clean; no source changes were needed.

detail.reason:
Shipped in commit 0c87c9e (src/hook.rs only, +143): relay artifact permission regression tests plus the fix they forced.

Finding: the promise was NOT held. HookInstaller::new never set a mode on the tempfile::Builder — the temp dir was created 0o777 & ~umask (0755 under umask 022, 0777 under a cleared umask), violating docs/notes/hook-design.md and plan T-1 (Stop payload readable by local users). mkfifo already requested 0600, which umask can only tighten.

Fix: Builder::permissions(0o700) so the dir is owner-only from the first instant, plus explicit set_permissions to 0700 (dir) / 0600 (FIFO) after creation — chmod is unconditional, so both modes hold verbatim under any umask, including restrictive ones (e.g. 0277 -> 0400) that would have broken hook.sh's FIFO write.

Tests added (src/hook.rs): temp_dir_mode_is_owner_only, fifo_mode_is_owner_rw, relay_artifact_modes_survive_usage (identity-relay write + FIFO round-trip, then re-assert both modes and fifo-ness), artifact_modes_hold_under_hostile_umask (umask 000 across HookInstaller::new, mirroring serve_socket_is_owner_only_regardless_of_umask in tests/serve.rs).

Counterfactual proof: the tests-only patch applied to pre-fix HEAD in a clean extraction — the three dir assertions FAILED (got 40755 normally, 40777 under umask 000) while the FIFO assertions passed, exactly the split the fix addresses; the tests catch the regression they exist for.

Added tests/sigwinch_forwarding_e2e.rs (sole change, commit 2542183, pushed to origin/main): hermetic e2e proving the PTY contract's SIGWINCH forwarding through the real PtySpawner::relay.

Coverage added (previously SIGINT-only per tests/sigint_forwarding_e2e.rs, whose SIGWINCH assertions pinned only the restore half):
- Child receives SIGWINCH: /bin/sh child with a WINCH trap records a marker only a delivered SIGWINCH can write; the kernel generates the child-side signal only when the PTY size actually CHANGES, so the trap firing proves relay consumed the parent-side signal and applied a different geometry.
- Geometry is forwarded: stty size inside the trap reads 50 200 from the child's own tty (resized from 24x80 via the test's fd-0 PTY, which relay reads as the parent stdin winsize).
- Dispositions restored: SIGINT and SIGWINCH back at SIG_DFL after relay returns; child reaped (second waitpid = ECHILD).

Also fixed a flake in the first draft found under real fleet load: the child originally wrote its readiness marker before arming the trap, so a forward landing in that window hit SIGWINCH's default-ignore disposition and was silently discarded (observed 5/5+ failures under concurrent builds; idle box passed). The committed script arms the trap first — program order makes the parent's readiness observation imply the armed disposition. Stability verified: 5 quiet runs + 6 runs under 8-spinner CPU contention, all green at ~0.13s; mutation test (forwarding disabled in pty.rs) fails loudly at the 15s supervision bound.
